Create a code-generated 2D cinematic animation for a mystery/documentary video.

SCENE

Narration:

“In the afternoon of November 24, 1971, a middle-aged man carrying a briefcase walked into Portland International Airport and purchased a one-way ticket to Seattle, Washington.”

The animation should visually communicate this exact sequence:

1. Portland International Airport exterior/interior is established.
2. A middle-aged man carrying a briefcase enters the airport.
3. He walks calmly through the airport.
4. He approaches the airline ticket counter.
5. He speaks to the ticket agent.
6. He purchases a one-way ticket to Seattle, Washington.
7. End with a subtle visual emphasis on the destination “SEATTLE” and the one-way ticket.

This is a historical mystery/documentary scene, so the animation should feel serious, restrained, atmospheric, and slightly mysterious rather than cartoonish or comedic.

⸻

VISUAL STYLE — VERY IMPORTANT

Use ONLY these primary visual elements:

* Background: PURE BLACK (#000000)
* Characters: RED (#FF2020 or similar)
* Important objects/details: RED
* Text: RED or very slightly brighter red
* No blue
* No green
* No yellow
* No realistic skin colors
* No gradients unless absolutely necessary
* No photographic textures
* No colorful airport environment

The entire animation should look like a sophisticated red-on-black minimalist motion graphic / silhouette animation.

Characters should be recognizable primarily through silhouettes and simple geometric shapes.

Think:

“1960s/1970s mystery documentary + minimalist cinematic silhouette + motion graphics.”

Do NOT make it look like a children’s cartoon.

⸻

CHARACTER DESIGN

Create one main character:

* Middle-aged man
* Male
* Average height
* Average build
* Wearing a dark 1971-style suit represented entirely with red silhouette/linework
* White shirt can be represented by black negative space
* Short, neat hairstyle
* No exaggerated facial features
* No smile
* Calm, neutral body language
* Carrying a rectangular briefcase in one hand

The man should immediately read as an ordinary middle-aged businessman/traveler.

Do not show a detailed face.

Use silhouette and posture to communicate his identity.

Create a second character:

* Airline ticket agent
* Standing/sitting behind a simple ticket counter
* Also rendered entirely in red silhouette/linework
* Minimal facial detail

⸻

AIRPORT DESIGN

Do not attempt to create a photorealistic airport.

Construct the airport using minimalist geometric shapes:

* Large rectangular terminal entrance
* Simple airport windows
* Ceiling lights represented by thin red lines
* Floor represented by subtle red perspective lines
* Simple signs
* Ticket counter
* Queue barrier
* A few distant passenger silhouettes

The airport should be recognizable without being visually busy.

Use strong negative space.

The black background should remain dominant.

⸻

CAMERA / COMPOSITION

Use a cinematic 16:9 composition.

The animation should NOT constantly change camera angles.

Use approximately 4–5 deliberate shots.

Each shot should last long enough for the viewer to understand what is happening.

Avoid rapid cuts.

Use smooth camera movement such as:

* slow horizontal tracking
* slow zoom
* subtle camera push-in
* simple cuts between major actions

The pacing should feel like a serious mystery documentary.

⸻

SHOT-BY-SHOT TIMELINE

Total duration: approximately 12–15 seconds.

SHOT 1 — AIRPORT ESTABLISHING SHOT

Duration: ~2.5 seconds

Start with a completely black screen.

Slowly reveal a minimalist red outline of an airport terminal.

Show:

PORTLAND INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT

as a small red sign or simple airport lettering.

Do not immediately reveal the entire airport.

Use a slow cinematic reveal.

A few tiny red passenger silhouettes can move in the distant background.

Camera slowly pushes toward the terminal entrance.

The scene should feel quiet and mysterious.

⸻

SHOT 2 — MAN ENTERS

Duration: ~3 seconds

Transition smoothly to the airport entrance.

The middle-aged man enters the frame from the LEFT.

He is carrying a rectangular briefcase in his right hand.

He walks from LEFT → RIGHT at a normal, relaxed walking speed.

His movement must look natural.

Animate:

* legs alternating naturally
* arms moving subtly
* briefcase moving slightly with each step
* body maintaining realistic balance

Do NOT make the walking cycle exaggerated.

Keep the man as a red silhouette against the black background.

Camera should track him slightly as he walks.

Other passengers may appear as very subtle distant red silhouettes, but the main man must remain the visual focus.

⸻

SHOT 3 — APPROACHING THE TICKET COUNTER

Duration: ~2.5 seconds

The man continues walking toward a simple ticket counter.

The camera slowly moves with him.

He reaches the counter.

He stops.

He places the briefcase naturally beside his leg or keeps holding it.

The airline agent is visible behind the counter.

The two figures face each other.

Hold this composition briefly.

Do not rush this moment.

⸻

SHOT 4 — BUYING THE TICKET

Duration: ~3 seconds

Show a medium shot of the man and ticket agent.

The agent gestures toward the ticket.

The man hands over money or payment.

The agent gives him a small rectangular ticket.

The man takes the ticket.

Use a subtle camera push-in toward the ticket.

The ticket should become visually important.

Keep everything red on black.

⸻

SHOT 5 — DESTINATION REVEAL

Duration: ~2–3 seconds

Transition to a close-up of the ticket in the man’s hand.

The ticket is represented as a simple red rectangular outline.

Display minimal text on the ticket:

ONE WAY

PORTLAND → SEATTLE

NOV 24, 1971

The word:

SEATTLE

should be slightly larger than the other text.

Do not make the text flashy.

After a brief pause, slowly fade everything back into black.

End on black.

⸻

ANIMATION QUALITY

The most important requirement is smoothness.

Use proper animation interpolation rather than abruptly changing positions.

Use:

* smooth easing
* linear motion where appropriate
* ease-in/ease-out for camera movements
* natural walking cycles
* subtle secondary motion

Avoid:

* jitter
* sudden position jumps
* robotic movement
* excessive motion
* fast cuts
* unnecessary particle effects
* flashy transitions

The animation should feel expensive and deliberate despite being generated with simple shapes.

⸻

CODE REQUIREMENTS

Generate the complete animation through code.

Prefer a deterministic vector/2D animation approach.

Use a resolution of:

1920 × 1080

and a 16:9 aspect ratio.

The animation must render to a standard video format such as MP4.

Use a consistent frame rate, preferably:

30 FPS.

Organize the code so that:

* scene timing is easy to modify
* colors are defined as variables
* character positions are defined clearly
* camera movement is separated from object animation
* each shot/scene has its own function
* the final render can be reproduced deterministically

For example, structure the code conceptually like:

scene_establishing_airport()
scene_man_enters()
scene_ticket_counter()
scene_purchase_ticket()
scene_ticket_closeup()

Do not hard-code everything into one enormous rendering function.

⸻

IMPORTANT VISUAL RESTRICTIONS

DO NOT generate:

* photorealistic people
* realistic airport photographs
* colorful backgrounds
* 3D cartoon characters
* anime characters
* exaggerated facial expressions
* comedy
* text-heavy screens
* unnecessary crowds
* modern airport branding
* modern smartphones
* modern clothing
* modern vehicles
* modern airport architecture

The scene represents November 24, 1971.

Everything visible should be visually compatible with the early 1970s.

⸻

HISTORICAL / NARRATIVE FEEL

The animation should NOT explicitly show the name “D.B. Cooper” yet.

The mystery should build naturally.

The viewer should simply see:

A middle-aged man.

A briefcase.

An airport.

A one-way ticket.

Seattle.

The scene should create the feeling that the viewer is watching an ordinary moment that will later become extremely important.

The final shot should leave a small sense of mystery.

⸻

FINAL RESULT

The finished animation should look like a professional minimalist true-crime / historical mystery documentary graphic.

Visual hierarchy:

BLACK BACKGROUND
↓
RED SILHOUETTES
↓
MIDDLE-AGED MAN
↓
BRIEFCASE
↓
AIRPORT
↓
ONE-WAY TICKET
↓
SEATTLE

Keep the animation clean, cinematic, restrained, and mysterious.

Do not add elements simply because they look visually interesting.

Every movement should support the narration.
